candidate: A Right to Delay an Answer: A Procedural Claim on Disclosure Timing
status: argument proposal; literature and originality unverified

claim.text: A participant in a legitimate shared-governance process may trigger a brief, pre-authorized neutral pause before organized disclosure when release would irreversibly foreclose a fair position-neutral procedure for a common decision.
scope_inclusions: defined participants whose standing is fixed independently of the answer
an inquiry operator with discretion over organized release
a concrete fair procedural option materially lost after disclosure
a pre-authorized bounded process with neutral review and a default
scope_exclusions: general right to ignorance or secrecy
veto over disclosure or choice of outcome
outsider disclosures outside the governed inquiry
situations where post-disclosure procedure restores equal standing

premises.text: Legitimate shared institutions can give defined participants equal standing over common decision procedures.
premises.needs_defense: What confers legitimacy and defines participants without using the answer to be disclosed?

premises.text: Some answers alter strategic positions and irreversibly remove an option to adopt a fair rule from a position-neutral standpoint.
premises.needs_defense: Show the lost option is real and cannot be restored by blind administration, simultaneous release, or post-disclosure review.

premises.text: Bypassing an authorized equal procedure can wrong participants even when no separate informational harm occurs and the outcome is unchanged.
premises.needs_defense: Establish the independent force of equal procedural standing; test reduction to consequence or established process rights.

premises.text: The claim is only to trigger a time-limited neutral procedure, not decide its result.
premises.needs_defense: Require prior authority, capped delay, review, and a default that prevents indefinite suppression.

premises.text: Urgent duties, necessary information, or a fully restorative less restrictive remedy defeat the claim.
premises.needs_defense: Specify how competing claims are assessed and who has authority.

inference: P1 identifies standing in an existing common procedure.
P2 identifies a particular irreversible timing loss.
P3 explains why that loss can matter apart from bad downstream outcomes.
P4 converts the concern into a bounded trigger right rather than a veto.
P5 supplies defeaters and proportionality limits.
Therefore a conditional procedural claim to a short hold may exist in this narrow class; no general right to postpone truth follows.
worked_case: Three co-beneficiaries share a collection. A harmless factual mapping shifts bargaining positions before they choose a division rule. An existing estate process gives any beneficiary one brief meeting, a neutral decider, and a default by deadline. A request pauses organized release only long enough to use that process.

assessor_engagement.source: Astra sketch assessment; explicitly attributed contribution astra-assessment-idea-003
assessor_engagement.challenge: What grounds standing when some reasonably reject the proposed fair procedure?
assessor_engagement.response: Standing derives from a legitimate pre-existing shared-governance rule independent of the answer. The claimant can trigger review, not impose the favored procedure. Without authority, neutral review, or a default, this argument supplies no unilateral hold.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Does the claim add anything beyond ordinary consequences, confidentiality, and contract?
assessor_engagement.response: These explain many cases. The proposed distinction is between who knows and when a shared decision rule is set. Institutional procedural standing may apply without an individually negotiated disclosure contract, but this may reduce to familiar procedural rights; originality remains unresolved.

strongest_objections: A neutral post-disclosure process may work as well; blind ex ante choice may be normatively irrelevant.
Information may reveal morally relevant needs and should change the rule.
A pause can empower dissenters to delay indefinitely or suppress evidence.
The account may be fully subsumed by confidentiality, contract, or established due-process rights.
replies: Require an actual irrecoverable procedural option and deny a hold where an alternative restores equal standing.
Exclude delay where the answer is needed to choose responsibly; neutral review may reject speculative claims.
Limit the trigger to an existing capped process with deadline, neutral decision-maker, default, and review.
Treat reduction to existing rights as a live falsifier, not an established novelty claim.
candidate_relation: Explicit descendant of the original idea candidate; narrows its broad timing thesis to a limited procedural trigger right within existing legitimate governance. The original candidate is retained as ancestry, not overwritten.
